name: Azithromycin
executiveSummary: Long half-life macrolide. Typical adult PO: **500 mg day 1 → 250 mg/day × 4 days** or **500 mg/day × 3 days**; Chlamydia STI: **1 g PO once**. Pediatrics: **10 mg/kg day 1 → 5 mg/kg × 4 days** (adult max). IV: **500 mg/day**.
indications:
## Indications

- Respiratory, ENT, skin infections (by susceptibility).
- Chlamydia / nongonococcal urethritis; some STI regimens.
- Mycobacterium avium (prophylaxis/treatment) in immunocompromised.
- Selected alternative in beta-lactam allergy.

## Precautions

- QT prolongation — avoid with other QT+/hypokalemia.
- Rare hepatotoxicity; C. difficile colitis.
- Separate from Al/Mg antacids ~2 h; interactions digoxin, warfarin, cyclosporine.

> Prefer PO; IV is a hospital bridge.

adulto.presentation: Tabs 250–500 mg; sachets/suspension; IV vial 500 mg.
adulto.dose: Classic respiratory: **500 mg PO day 1**, then **250 mg/day × 4 days**; or **500 mg/day × 3 days**. Pneumonia/hospital: **500 mg PO/IV every 24 h**. Chlamydia: **1 g PO once**. MAC prophylaxis: **1.2 g PO once weekly** (regimens).
adulto.administration: PO 1 h before or 2 h after meals (better fasting absorption on many labels). IV: infuse 1–3 h by concentration (no bolus).

pediatrico.dose: Otitis/respiratory ≥6 mo: **10 mg/kg PO day 1** (max **500 mg**), then **5 mg/kg/day × 4 days** (max **250 mg**); or **10 mg/kg/day × 3 days** (max 500). Strep pharyngitis (if used): **12 mg/kg/day × 5 days** (max 500). Adolescent STI: **1 g PO once**. <6 mo: per label/indication (e.g. 10 mg/kg/day × 5).

neonatal.dose: Restricted use (e.g. congenital Chagas / ophthalmia schemes) — neonatology only.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted suspension: per label (often 5–10 days refrigerated or room temp).
- IV: use dilution within manufacturer window.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, headache; rare: hepatitis, long QT, hypersensitivity, C. difficile.
